The proposed answer is correct.

**Speed.** Differentiating gives f'(θ) = ie^{iθ}(1+e^{iθ})², so |f'(θ)| = |1+e^{iθ}|² = 2 + 2cos θ. The total arc length over [0, 2π] is therefore 4π.

**Self-intersection.** At θ = 2π/3 and θ = 4π/3, f = ω + ω² + 1/3 = −1 + 1/3 = −2/3, so the curve crosses itself there. The cusp is at θ = π, where f = −1/3.

**Which part is the boundary.** The inner loop (θ from 2π/3 to 4π/3) runs from −2/3 to the cusp at −1/3 and back, so it lies inside the large outer loop. The tangent directions at −2/3 confirm this: the curve arrives heading right-down and the outer arc leaves heading left-down. The boundary of R is therefore the outer loop, covering θ ∈ [0, 2π/3] ∪ [4π/3, 2π].

**Length.** The inner loop has length ∫_{2π/3}^{4π/3} (2 + 2cos θ) dθ = 4π/3 + 2(sin(4π/3) − sin(2π/3)) = 4π/3 − 2√3. The outer loop is the remainder: 4π − (4π/3 − 2√3) = 8π/3 + 2√3 ≈ 8.3776 + 3.4641 = 11.8417.

This matches the stated final answer of 11.8417.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
